article_title: I quit my £80,000 job to make ice cream - here's how

tasks.prompt: What is the main purpose of Vivien Wong's story?
options: To explain how she and her brother built the Little Moons mochi ice-cream business and what founders can learn from it
To argue that accounting qualifications are useless
To review every ice-cream brand sold in Britain
To announce that Little Moons has stopped manufacturing
tasks.correct_answer: To explain how she and her brother built the Little Moons mochi ice-cream business and what founders can learn from it
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה משתמשת במסלול של ויוויאן וונג כדי להסביר בניית עסק ואת הלקחים ליזמים.

tasks.prompt: What job did Wong leave at the age of 28?
options: A £20,000 restaurant job
An £80,000-a-year accounting job
A teaching job in Japan
A supermarket management role
tasks.explanation_hebrew: וונג עזבה בגיל 28 משרת ראיית חשבון ששילמה 80 אלף ליש״ט בשנה.

tasks.prompt: What does “reinvest” mean in the context of a growing company?
options: To return earnings to the business to support further growth
To hide all company income from retailers
To replace a product with an identical one
To borrow money without a plan
tasks.correct_answer: To return earnings to the business to support further growth
tasks.explanation_hebrew: reinvest פירושו להשקיע רווחים בחזרה בעסק כדי לפתח אותו.

tasks.prompt: What product did Vivien and Howard Wong create?
options: Traditional bread filled with red bean paste
A drink made from melted ice cream
A mochi snack filled with ice cream
A machine for supermarket freezers
tasks.correct_answer: A mochi snack filled with ice cream
tasks.explanation_hebrew: האחים הקימו את Little Moons סביב מוצ׳י – בצק רך העוטף גלידה.

tasks.prompt: Why did the founders first sell to restaurants before focusing on supermarkets?
options: Restaurant customers were more willing to try an unfamiliar Japanese dessert
Supermarkets were legally forbidden to sell frozen food
Restaurants supplied all of the company's machinery
The founders wanted the product to remain unknown
tasks.correct_answer: Restaurant customers were more willing to try an unfamiliar Japanese dessert
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מסעדות אפשרו לצרכנים לנסות מוצר לא מוכר, וההצלחה שם נתנה לקניינים ביטחון.

tasks.prompt: When the article warns founders not to follow a trend “blindly”, what does it mean?
options: Promote a product only with photographs
Copy a popular idea without examining whether it fits the business
Avoid speaking to colleagues
Manufacture every product by hand
tasks.correct_answer: Copy a popular idea without examining whether it fits the business
tasks.explanation_hebrew: blindly כאן פירושו ללכת אחרי טרנד בלי לבדוק התאמה, סיכונים ונסיבות.

tasks.prompt: Give three early challenges the Wong siblings faced while building Little Moons.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שלושה אתגרים עסקיים או תפעוליים מן הכתבה.
expected_points: They had to develop a product category unfamiliar in the UK
There was no suitable European machinery or supplier for scaled production
They invested personal savings and kept costs lean
Retailers did not know where the product belonged in the freezer aisle
They had to persuade distributors and buyers to take a chance on an unknown brand
Manufacturing warm mochi dough around frozen ice cream required experimentation

tasks.prompt: Summarise how Little Moons moved from an idea to a widely recognised brand.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול את הרעיון, הפיתוח, המכירה הראשונית והצמיחה.
expected_points: Vivien and Howard discovered ice-cream-filled mochi abroad
They left their jobs and developed the product
They used family bakery space and invested in machinery
They first built demand through restaurants
Retail listings and a long-running Selfridges pop-up increased visibility
TikTok attention during the pandemic sharply accelerated demand
Years of groundwork preceded the apparent overnight success

tasks.prompt: Why does Wong say a polished brand is not enough to make a business succeed?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להבחין בין מראה שיווקי לבין יסודות עסקיים.
expected_points: Branding can attract attention but cannot replace a good product
Founders need reliable manufacturing and infrastructure
They must understand customers and retailers
Cash must be managed and often reinvested
Growth depends on repeated problem-solving, not appearance alone

tasks.prompt: Using Wong's experience, advise an aspiring founder on when to take a career risk and how to reduce that risk.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לנסח עצה מאוזנת המבוססת על דוגמאות מן הכתבה.
expected_points: Clarify the personal reason for changing career
Test whether customers want the product
Use available resources, as the siblings used bakery space
Keep costs lean and reinvest carefully
Build manufacturing capacity before rapid growth
Do not follow trends blindly
Be cautious about individual circumstances and financial security
Commit fully only after evaluating the risks
